comment: Shared wardrobe vectors (docs/design/purse-and-wardrobe.md 4.2). Two sets, replayed by different sides — pick the right one. `resolve` is server only (lane C, server/internal/rules): resolve(chosen, owned, catalog) drops a chosen key the player no longer owns (a lapsed piece) or the catalog no longer knows, and keeps the rest — the stored row survives, only the resolved choice shrinks, so a piece that comes back returns to its place. Its cases pin their own `catalog` list so a key added upstream later can never flip an expectation. `lookFor` is shared by both sides (lane C's rules.Look and lane E's src/lib/wardrobe.ts): lookFor(profile, chosen) exactly as 4.2, for each drawn slot (the `slots` list) — chosen[slot] == "none" -> null; chosen[slot] is a key -> that key; otherwise profile.useCostume ? profile.costume[slot] : profile.equipped[slot]. `chosen` arrives already resolved (PlayerState.wardrobe is the resolved choice), so this set has no owned list. A missing profile key resolves to null (nothing worn there); a *_base_0 key is returned as a key and draws nothing downstream; weaponSpecial is never drawn and never appears. The avatar's own rules apply after lookFor, unchanged: a two-handed weapon hides the shield (the two-handed case keeps both keys in the look and says so).

resolve.name: owned-and-catalogued-stays
resolve.note: Owned keys the catalog knows hold their slots; the reserved 'none' (Nothing) is kept — it can never collide with a Habitica key.

resolve.name: a-lapsed-key
resolve.note: The head piece is no longer owned (a lapsed key): it drops out of the resolved choice and the slot reads As on Habitica until it is back. The stored row stays; only the resolution shrinks.

resolve.name: an-uncatalogued-key
resolve.note: A key the catalog no longer (or never) knew drops out even when it is owned: an unknown key can't be drawn.

resolve.name: nothing-chosen-resolves-to-nothing
resolve.note: No rows at all: the whole choice is As on Habitica.

lookFor.name: as-on-habitica
lookFor.note: Nothing chosen: the battle gear, slots it has nothing for left null, the *_base_0 none-pieces kept as keys (they draw nothing).

lookFor.name: as-on-habitica-costume
lookFor.note: Show costume is on at Habitica: As on Habitica means the costume, exactly what Habitica shows.

lookFor.name: a-chosen-key-beats-the-costume
lookFor.note: useCostume true with one chosen slot: the choice wins there (the battle gear's helm, not the costume's bicorne); every other slot still reads the costume.

lookFor.name: none
lookFor.note: The reserved 'none' choice is Nothing worn there, whatever Habitica shows; the unchosen slots stay as on Habitica.

lookFor.name: a-chosen-key
lookFor.note: A piece chosen for its slot wins over the Habitica look there and nowhere else. (Whether the player still owns it is resolve's business, not this function's.)

lookFor.name: two-handed-weapon-over-a-chosen-shield
lookFor.note: The staff (weapon_wizard_1) is two-handed (the catalog's twoHanded) and the shield is chosen beside it: lookFor keeps both keys — the avatar's own rule hides the shield when it draws (src/lib/habitica/avatar.ts; the same on the server's visualAvatar), and the wardrobe stays chosen, so putting a one-handed weapon back shows the shield again.
